title: 3D Change of Basis and Linear Combinations
full_prompt: Write a ManimGL script that visualizes a 3D change of basis. First, set up a 3D scene with a slowly rotating camera frame. Add 3D axes, a coordinate plane, and three standard basis vectors colored Red, Green, and Blue for the X, Y, and Z axes respectively. Introduce a yellow 'Signal' vector with a dynamic label showing its current position. Calculate and display the linear combination components (projected vectors stacked tip-to-tail) that dynamically update to match the signal vector. Animate the initial construction of these components using a transform from the basis vectors. Then, animate the signal vector moving to several different 3D coordinates, showing how the components dynamically stretch and update. Next, perform a change of basis by rotating the basis vectors to a new set of orthogonal directions (using a rotation matrix). Show how the components dynamically adapt and project onto this new coordinate system as the signal vector moves to a new position.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Using Manim Community camera methods on ManimGL camera frame
common_failure_modes.note: ManimGL uses self.camera.frame.reorient() and self.camera.frame.add_updater() instead of self.set_camera_orientation().
In 3D scenes, depth testing must be explicitly applied to mobjects to prevent rendering overlap issues.
